title: AI-Powered Personal Knowledge Hub
summary: A note-taking app with an AI layer: write rich notes with attachments, then ask questions and get answers grounded in your own notes, with numbered citations that jump to the exact passage or PDF page. It works with no AI key at all, through a built-in AI running self-hosted open-source models under Free and Pro plans, and users can plug in their own OpenRouter, Gemini, OpenAI or Claude key for stronger models.
challenge: AI answers over personal notes are only useful if people can trust them and afford them. Every answer had to point back to its sources, editing a note shouldn't mean paying to re-embed everything, and the app had to work for users who have no AI key.
desc: Split the system into four services: Next.js web app, NestJS API (orchestration, search index, background indexing), Express file storage, and a stateless FastAPI + LangChain AI service that extracts, chunks, embeds and generates.

Built a MongoDB-backed indexing queue with atomic job claims, retry with backoff and stale-lock recovery; content hashes make re-indexing incremental, so an edit re-embeds only the changed passages and attachments are never read twice.
Implemented hybrid retrieval: Atlas Vector Search plus keyword search, merged with reciprocal rank fusion, with an in-API cosine fallback and automatic query rewriting when the first search is weak.
Designed RAG answers with numbered citations that open the source note scrolled to the highlighted passage, or the attachment at the cited page; chat searches notes and past conversations together.

Added a built-in AI that needs no key (Qwen3.5 4B + Qwen3-Embedding via Ollama) with Free/Pro plans: per-session token allowances, a priority queue that puts questions ahead of indexing, and one-time voucher codes for upgrades.

Supported four AI providers with live model lists, one-click OpenRouter connect (OAuth PKCE) and API keys encrypted at rest; vectors are labelled by embedding model so switching providers rebuilds them from stored text.

Reads PDFs (including scanned pages and images via vision models) and DOCX; generates brief or action-item summaries (tasks, owners, deadlines, decisions), cached per note; Google sign-in and an installable PWA.

title: Offline-First Farm Harvest & Pack Management System

caseStudy.title: Overview
caseStudy.content: A production-grade Progressive Web App designed for field operations in environments with unreliable or no internet connectivity.

caseStudy.title: Problem
caseStudy.content: Field users frequently operate without stable connectivity, leading to failed API calls, partial submissions, and inconsistent system state in traditional online-only architectures.

caseStudy.title: Solution
caseStudy.content: Designed an offline-first architecture using IndexedDB for durable client-side storage and an outbox pattern to queue write operations. Connectivity listeners trigger background sync, while idempotent backend APIs safely replay queued requests.

caseStudy.title: Key Engineering Highlights
content: Centralized sync state using store patterns

caseStudy.title: Results & Impact
content: Improved perceived performance for field users
Significant reduction in sync-related support issues
Successfully used in daily production workflows

title: CareConnect - Hospital Management System
desc: Engineered a low-latency chat module using SignalR, supporting 1:1 and group messaging.
Implemented granular RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) for Admins, Physicians, and Patients using JWT.
Designed a normalized PostgreSQL schema optimized for complex medical history queries.
Built end-to-end document handling for secure prescription uploads.
summary: A real-time, secure hospital ecosystem built for scale.
challenge: Most hospital systems are fragmented, forcing users to switch between tools. The goal was to engineer a unified ecosystem that seamlessly handles three distinct, conflicting workflows (Admin oversight, Physician diagnostics, and Patient booking) within a single secure interface using JWT authentication.
